changelog: The firewall can now ask which network the phone is on instead of only which address connects. /data/adb/modules/adb_wifi/config gains GATE (subnet | ssid, default subnet), TRUSTED_SSIDS and TRUSTED_BSSIDS. GATE=ssid closes the port to everyone while wlan0 is on a network that is on neither list and opens it as usual once it is, so a cafe that hands out your home range gets nothing; LAN_SUBNETS still decides who is admitted inside a trusted network. The name and the radio address are read from iw dev wlan0 link on every wlan0 address or link event, so moving to another network closes the port within a moment without a reboot, and an interface that is not associated counts as untrusted. GATE=ssid refuses to start with a FATAL when neither list is filled or iw is missing, and every rewrite logs the network it decided on, so a name that does not match says so instead of leaving the port shut unexplained. Measured on the device and fixed in the same release: ip monitor exits when it is pointed at an interface that does not exist yet, and at boot that is what closed the event stream and left the port shut until something restarted the watcher, so the watcher now waits for the interface and restarts the source whenever it goes away, while its reader survives the gap between restarts instead of ending with it. The stream itself was trimmed to the three message types that can mean a network changed, address, link and route, because ip monitor all also reports every neighbour entry and routing rule a busy LAN and a phone churn through, and each of those used to cost a full re-read of the network. The boot log also carries a WARNING when service.adb.tls.port is not 0, because Android's own Wireless debugging is a listener this fence does not know about and only Developer options can silence it. Defaults and behaviour for existing configs are unchanged. A gate on the peer's own hardware address was measured and dropped: iptables -m mac needs net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables, and a kernel without br_netfilter never hands hardware addresses to the IP hooks, so on this device the rule installs and a peer presenting exactly the listed MAC is still rejected because it never matches. This release fails closed where it used to fail open: the fence is read back before adbd is told to listen, so a jump or a REJECT rule that did not install stops the script with a FATAL instead of leaving the port open to everyone, and config values are validated the way iptables validates them, so a wrong prefix length or an address of the wrong family is a FATAL at boot rather than a rule that is silently missing. The watcher also stops waiting for an address once it has an event stream, so the port closes the moment the address goes away instead of forty seconds later, and run/watch.pid is only acted on when the process behind it really is the watcher. 6.1 is 6.0 with the versionCode bumped, so a device holding the first 6.0 build is offered the same module in-app.
